Branch.description:
A branch as the API shows it. `host` and `port` only for a ready `normal` branch with an
endpoint.

history_start.description: Where the branch's history begins (null when unknown); Studio's lower bound for a point.

main_database_missing.description:
A ready branch with no recorded main database: it was dropped in SQL. The data API is
unavailable on the branch until a database of the main name exists again.

protected.description:
A protected branch can't be deleted or reset to its parent (restore still works), and
its database can't be deleted. Set with `updateBranch`.

BranchDatabaseView.description: A Postgres database of a branch.

main.description: The branch's main database: the one the data API serves.

owner.description: The Postgres role that owns it.

BranchId.description: Stable identifier for a branch of a database; main's equals its database id.

BranchRole.description: A role of a branch, without secrets. The owner comes first.

blocked_keys.description:
Live data API secret keys that name this role while it is owner-level: the keys the
data API refuses (empty for a plain role).

level.description:
`owner_level`: superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION, or a member of
`neon_superuser` at any depth. Such a role can't back a data API secret key.

login.description: Whether the role has the LOGIN attribute.

origin.description: The branch's owner, a role made in SQL, or one made through the API.

password.description:
Whether the password can be shown (`generated`), was set in SQL, or is an unusable MD5
hash.

pending.description: Written but not yet applied to the compute; applied when the compute next runs.

enum.description: Qualified enum name (`schema.name`) when the column is an enum.

ConnectionDetails.description: How to connect to a branch as one of its roles.

ca_file.description:
Self-hosted mode only: the file holding the dev proxy's CA certificate, for
`sslrootcert=` (the URI keeps `sslmode=verify-full`). Null in platform mode.

password.description: Null when it can't be shown; `password_state` says why.

password_state.description:
`generated`: made by Cheladb, shown here. `set_in_sql`: set in SQL, only its hash is
stored; reset it to get a shown one. `md5_unusable`: an MD5 hash, which Cheladb's proxy
can't use; set a new password. `unreadable`: the stored password could not be opened
(a rename or branch copy dropped it); reset it.

uri.description:
Without a password when `password` is null. The user and database are
percent-encoded.

oneOf.description: A point in the parent's history; its present when omitted.
The branch to start from; main when omitted.

owner_level.description:
Makes the role owner-level, like the branch owner: CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, BYPASSRLS
and REPLICATION, and a member of `neon_superuser`. Default `false`.

CreatedDataKey.description: A key just made, with its plaintext.

DataApiSchema.description: The Data API schema: everything the asking roles can reach.

DataKey.description: A key as listed: `key` only for the public key.

role_blocked.description:
A secret key whose role is owner-level: the data API refuses it. Always false for the
public key.

branch_count.description: Live `normal` branches, main included (backups and deleted branches don't count).

history_window.description: Seconds of history the database keeps.

DatabaseId.description: Stable identifier for a provisioned database instance.

DatabaseSettings.description: A database's settings after a change.

history_window.description: Seconds of history the database keeps.

DatabaseSummary.description: Public database fields only: never credentials or container ids.

ErrorBody.description:
The documented shape of the `error` object. Some codes add extra keys (for example
`keys`), which are documented per code.

ErrorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable error code. Serialises as snake_case.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The schema error responses reference: `{"error": ErrorBody}`.

oneOf.description: `None` when the caller's org isn't bound to a Cheladb tenant yet.

OperationAccepted.description: The 202 body of the routes that start background work: the status the row moved to.

PasswordState.description: Where a role's password stands, as Studio shows it.

PointInTime.description: Where in a branch's history: exactly one of a time or an LSN.

ProjectId.description: Stable identifier for a project within a tenant.

RestoreAccepted.description:
The 202 body of a restore: the branch is `resetting`, and its previous state is kept as a
backup branch.

backup_branch_id.description: The backup branch holding the state before the restore.

at.description: The point in the branch's history to rewind to.

RoleInUseKey.description: A data API key that names an owner-level role; also the `keys` extra of `role_in_use`.

RoleLevel.description:
What a role may do: `OwnerLevel` is the wide definition (superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB,
BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION, or `neon_superuser` at any depth).

RoleOrigin.description:
Where a `neon_roles` row came from: the branch's owner, a role made in SQL, or one made
through the API.

SchemaEntry.description: One schema's tables, functions (overloads by name) and enums (labels by name).

TableDesc.description: A table, view or foreign table. `privileges` (role to held privileges) is `null` unless asked for.

protected.description:
`true` refuses deleting the branch, resetting it to its parent and deleting its
database; restore still works.

UpdateDatabaseRequest.description: All optional; a missing one is left as it is. `history_window` is in seconds.
